q-17533.prompt_mask:
Consider the following first-order linear ODE for the function $y=y(x):$

$$
x\frac{dy}{dx}+xy=@R@
$$

Write the equation in the form $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(yI(x))=I(x)Q(x),$ where $I(x)$ is an integrating factor.
q-17533.solution_mask:
First, we write the equation in standard form. This gives

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+y=@Q@.
$$

This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)
$$

with $P(x)=1$ and $Q(x)=@Q@.$ We proceed to find an integrating factor $I(x)$ using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,dx} \\  & ={e}^{\int 1\,dx} \\  & ={e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply our differential equation through by $I(x)={e}^{x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\cdot (\frac{dy}{dx}+y) & ={e}^{x}\cdot @Q@ \\ {e}^{x}\frac{dy}{dx}+{e}^{x}y & ={e}^{x}\cdot @Q@\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the left hand side as $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y\cdot I(x)):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}(y{e}^{x}) & ={e}^{x}\cdot @Q@\end{aligned}
$$

q-17539.prompt_mask:
Consider the following first-order linear ODE for the function $y=y(x):$

$$
{x}^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}+xy={x}^{2}@Q@,\,x>0
$$

Write the equation in the form $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(yI(x))=I(x)Q(x),$ where $I(x)$ is an integrating factor.
q-17539.solution_mask:
First, we write the equation in standard form. This gives

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}\cdot y=@Q@.
$$

This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)
$$

with $P(x)=\frac{1}{x}$ and $Q(x)=@Q@.$ We proceed to find an integrating factor $I(x)$ using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)dx} \\  & ={e}^{\int (1/x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x} \\  & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply our differential equation through by $I(x)=x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}\cdot y) & =x\cdot @Q@ \\ x\cdot \frac{dy}{dx}+y & =x@Q@\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the left hand side as $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y\cdot I(x)):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}(yx) & =x@Q@.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we write the equation in standard form. This gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\frac{2}{x}\cdot y=@Q@.

$$
